pages.task: The axis of `y = x² + 6x + 5` is at `x = −3`, and each arrow is 2 long. What are the roots of `x² + 6x + 5 = 0`?
pages.why: The roots sit the same distance either side of the axis, so they are `−3 + 2` and `−3 − 2`, which are −1 and −5. Put back into the rule, `1 − 6 + 5 = 0` and `25 − 30 + 5 = 0`.

pages.alt: y equals ax squared plus bx plus c. The curve of the rule is drawn. The dashed axis is at x equals minus b divided by 2a. Two equal arrows reach out from the axis to the roots. ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0. a(x plus b divided by 2a) squared plus c minus b squared divided by 4a equals 0. (x plus b divided by 2a) squared equals (b squared minus 4ac) divided by 4a squared. x plus b divided by 2a equals plus or minus root (b squared minus 4ac) divided by 2a. x equals ( minus b plus or minus root (b squared minus 4ac)) divided by 2a. centre minus b divided by 2a, spread root (b squared minus 4ac) divided by 2a.

pages.why: Line 2 put only the square root over 2. The whole top goes over `2a`, so `x = (−6 ± 4) ÷ 2`, which is −1 or −5, and `1 − 6 + 5 = 0`.

pages.task: What are the roots of `3x² + 5x − 1 = 0`, to two decimal places?
pages.why: No whole-number pair works here, so the formula is the quick way. `b² − 4ac` is `25 + 12 = 37`, and `√37` is about 6.08, so `x = (−5 ± 6.08) ÷ 6`, about 0.18 or −1.85. Put back, `3 × 0.18² + 5 × 0.18 − 1` is −0.0028, which is 0 but for the rounding. On a calculator, type the bottom in brackets, `÷ (2 × 3)`; without them it divides by 2, then multiplies by 3.

pages.why: All three have `b² = 16`. For `x² − 4x + 5`, `b² − 4ac` is `16 − 20 = −4`, so there are no real roots. Its roots are [[complex numbers]], numbers off the number line, which the Complex numbers course takes up.
